newsitem.title: UK: Marks & Spencer up in firm retail sector.
newsitem.headline: Marks & Spencer up in firm retail sector.

text.p: Shares in Marks & Spencer and other major UK retail groups rose on Thursday after a mostly upbeat report on prospects for consumer spending in 1997, dealers said.

The survey, by economic consultancy Business Strategies Ltd, said consumer spending in the UK was likely to rise 4.5 percent this year, the fastest rate since the recession at the beginning of the 1990s, though growth in consumer confidence had slowed.
"The Business Strategies report was pretty strong so we have seen a bit of a recovery in the retail stocks," said one dealer.
Shares in M&S were up 9p at 491, recovering from yesterday's 11p drop after a Christmas trading statement fell short of some expectations.
Other leading retail stocks were also higher, with Great Universal Stores Plc up 16p at 640-1/2, Dixons Group Plc up 12p at 507 and Argos Plc up 7p at 645.
